prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1320; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a low-speed head-on collision reported by the insured. Insured states the other vehicle crossed into the lane during a merge. No police report filed at scene. Both drivers reported neck pain at the scene but declined transport. Vehicle inspection scheduled.

Entry 2: Field inspection completed on the insured vehicle. Front bumper cover cracked, hood latch misaligned, minor radiator support damage. Photos uploaded to file. Repair estimate requested from preferred shop. Claimant's vehicle not yet inspected.

Entry 3: Claimant has retained counsel. Attorney letter of representation received and logged. All further contact with the claimant to be routed through counsel. Request for medical records and treatment history sent to attorney's office. Liability position under review pending witness statement.

Entry 4: Claimant's attorney submitted initial treatment records showing diagnosis of whiplash-type cervical strain. Chiropractic care reported, with physical therapy referral noted. Records reviewed. Reserve adjusted to reflect bodily injury exposure. Requested itemized billing and any prior neck complaints for the past several years.

Entry 5: Liability assessment updated. Based on the insured's statement, the independent witness account, and vehicle damage pattern, the other driver appears primarily at fault. Subrogation notice prepared for the at-fault carrier. Claim remains open pending receipt of final medical billing and repair invoices. Supervisor review scheduled.
